prompt: Our Qdrant search was running fine at around 20ms per query last week, but now it's taking 200-300ms. We didn't change any config. We're running Qdrant 1.12 on an SSD-backed cluster with about 2M vectors at 768 dimensions. We did a big data upload over the weekend though. What could be causing this?

assertions.name: classified_as_regression_pattern
assertions.description: Explicitly classified as a performance regression pattern (Phase 3D or equivalent)
assertions.check: Response explicitly identifies this as a regression/degradation pattern, not a general 'slow search' issue. Must route to the correct diagnostic branch.

assertions.name: ordered_diagnosis_correctly
assertions.description: Checked optimizer status FIRST, then segments, then cache, then data growth
assertions.check: Response checks causes in the correct priority order: optimizer running > unmerged segments > cache eviction > data growth. Optimizer must be checked before any config recommendations.

assertions.name: warned_against_config_changes_during_optimizer
assertions.description: Explicitly warned not to make config changes while optimizer is running
assertions.check: Response contains an explicit warning against changing configuration (HNSW params, quantization, etc.) while the optimizer is still running

assertions.name: referenced_qdrant_docs
assertions.description: Included links to specific Qdrant documentation pages
assertions.check: Response contains at least one URL linking to qdrant.tech documentation

assertions.name: suggested_future_upload_workflow
assertions.description: Provided a recommended workflow for future bulk uploads to prevent this
assertions.check: Response suggests a preventive workflow for future uploads (e.g., disable indexing during upload, then re-enable; or upload during low-traffic windows)
